properties.description:
Take a directory of written specifications and produce one coherent design from the whole corpus, keeping each claim's provenance Fragment pointing back at its source document. Extends single-document extraction with the four things a corpus needs and one file does not: ONE epoch for the whole run (left alone, ingest opens an epoch per document and 500 files read as 500 unrelated events); one Fragment per document; identity resolution ACROSS documents, so the same thing named in many specs converges on one node; and the ambiguous near-match band gathered across the whole corpus and deduplicated into ONE question, because dec:ask-not-repair at corpus scale means the asking must be batched or the feature is unusable.

BUILT 2026-08-05 (BL-186), as `ingest_corpus_step` over `corpus.rs`, plus the served `ingest-corpus` skill that walks the folder — reflow2 performs no file I/O, so the agent reads the files and the graph records what came of them and an opaque locator back (dec:agent-navigates-content).

TWO PROPERTIES WORTH STATING BECAUSE THEY ARE NOT OBVIOUS FROM THE NAME. (1) THE HANDSHAKE BATCHES ACROSS DOCUMENTS: prompts for every document are gathered into one round, so a corpus costs the ~3 rounds a single document costs rather than 3N. That works because a prompt's id is a hash of its semantic content, so one shared answer pool cannot cross-feed documents and two identical documents are answered once — no new mechanism was needed. The document text still crosses the agent's context once per prompt, and that cost is NOT solved here. (2) RESUME IS DERIVED, NEVER BOOKMARKED: a document whose fragment_id already exists comes back `skipped` rather than failed, so re-running over a grown folder ingests only what is new and "what is left" is computed by asking the graph. That depends entirely on the caller deriving fragment_id from the path — the served skill says so in the strongest terms it has, because generating ids afresh re-ingests the whole corpus every time and looks like it worked.

THE LIMIT ON THE RECORD: convergence is LEXICAL. token_sort_ratio catches `Auth Service` ~ `Authentication Service` and cannot see `Read Cache` ~ `Local Store` at all — not a low score, invisible. So convergence holds for documents that share vocabulary, which a corpus written by many authors over years often does not. Whether to close that with embeddings is open (dec:idea-embeddings-adoption). The evidence scope on this capability's check records the same limit mechanically: `corpus_size` and `vocabulary_overlap` are PINNED, so the passing check proves the behaviour at three documents that share words, not at 1,124 that do not.
properties.name: Ingest a folder of specifications as one design
